news.headline_zh: 禽流感病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期禽流感病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 新南威尔士州第一产业和区域发展部 (NSW DPIRD) 与澳大利亚政府合作报告称,新南威尔士州三个地点的四个 野生鸟类 已确认检测到 H5 禽流感 (H5N1)。该事件已得到证实并正在调查中。 [news-79627a5814fdb790]
能源、环境和气候行动部 (DEECA) 已确认凯西市发现一例 H5 禽流感病例;由凯西市作为官方议会新闻报道;事件已确认。 [news-4f571d7ea7fc82d9]
H5N1 高致病性禽流感 已进入澳大利亚,自 2026 年 6 月起在野生海鸟中得到证实,有记录表明对标志性和濒危本土动物存在风险,并且未来可能传播到家禽;澳大利亚政府正在启动针对圈养濒危物种的 疫苗接种 行动。 [news-e6b1815b000ab37e]
南澳大利亚内陆地区发现了禽流感(H5N1),距离罗布100多公里处报告了新病例,罗布一直是澳大利亚禽流感的焦点地区暴发。野生动物专家和鸟类饲养者呼吁 疫苗 保护濒危物种和私人鸟类。 [news-e98445524df913f9]
在澳大利亚首次记录大规模鸟类 死亡率 事件后,澳大利亚卫生当局和 CSIRO 专家评估 H5N1 禽流感 死亡率 从鸟类传播到人类的风险“非常低”。据报道,该事件正在调查中并持续监测。 [news-076f0fc61f788633]

news.headline_en: Recent Avian influenza A viruses news
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Avian influenza A viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: Confirmed detection of H5 bird flu (H5N1) in four wild birds across three NSW locations, reported by the NSW Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (NSW DPIRD) in partnership with the Australian Government. The event is confirmed and under investigation. [news-79627a5814fdb790]

The Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action (DEECA) has confirmed that the City of Casey has recorded a case of H5 bird flu; reported by the City of Casey as official council news; event is confirmed. [news-4f571d7ea7fc82d9]

H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza has entered Australia, confirmed in wild seabirds since June 2026, with documented risk to iconic and endangered native fauna and potential future spread to poultry; Australian government is initiating targeted vaccination of captive endangered species. [news-e6b1815b000ab37e]

Bird flu (H5N1) has been detected inland in South Australia, with reports of new cases more than 100 kilometres from Robe, which has been a focal point of Australia's bird flu outbreak. Wildlife experts and bird keepers are calling for vaccines to protect at-risk species and privately owned birds. [news-e98445524df913f9]

Australian health authorities and CSIRO experts assess the risk of H5N1 avian influenza transmission from birds to humans as 'very low' following Australia’s first recorded mass bird mortality event. The event is reported as under investigation with ongoing monitoring. [news-076f0fc61f788633]

papers.title: Protective effect of A(H5N8) stockpiled vaccine against a virus genetically identical to a human isolate of bovine A(H5N1) influenza virus.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Since early 2024, highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses of clade 2.3.4.4b have caused extensive outbreaks in dairy cattle in the United States, with spillover into mammalian species, including humans. A bovine-derived A(H5N1) virus isolated from a human case retains high pathogenicity and transmissibility in mammalian models, highlighting its pandemic potential. Stockpiled pre-pandemic influenza vaccines are intended to provide early protection before strain-matched vaccines are available; however, their protective efficacy against bovine A(H5N1) viruses has not been directly evaluated in vivo. METHODS: In this study, we assessed the protective efficacy of an AS03-adjuvanted A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (H5N8) clade 2.3.4.4b-based influenza vaccine stockpiled in Japan using mouse and ferret models. Vaccinated and unvaccinated animals were challenged with a virus genetically identical to a human isolate of bovine A(H5N1) virus. Neutralising antibody responses, viral replication in organs, and survival were evaluated. FINDINGS: Vaccination with the AS03-adjuvanted A(H5N8)-based stockpiled vaccine induced robust neutralising antibody responses in both animal models, significantly suppressed viral replication, and conferred complete protection against lethal challenge. In contrast, all unvaccinated mice and ferrets succumbed to infection. These findings demonstrate that the AS03-adjuvanted A(H5N8)-based stockpiled vaccine provides strong cross-protective efficacy against bovine A(H5N1) viruses. INTERPRETATION: An AS03-adjuvanted A(H5N8)-based vaccine stockpiled in Japan could serve as an immediate countermeasure against bovine A(H5N1) viruses during the early phase of a pandemic. FUNDING: This work was supported by grants from the Japan Program for Infectious Diseases Research and Infrastructure (JP20wm0125002) and the Japan Initiative for World-leading Vaccine Research and Development Centers (JP223fa627001) from the Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development.

analysis.methods: The study evaluated neutralising antibody responses, viral replication in organs, and survival in both vaccinated and unvaccinated animal models. analysis.main_results: Vaccination with the AS03-adjuvanted A(H5N8)-based stockpiled vaccine induced robust neutralising antibody responses in both animal models, significantly suppressed viral replication, and conferred complete protection against lethal challenge. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that stockpiled A(H5N8)-based vaccines may offer protection against related bovine A(H5N1) viruses, which could inform pandemic preparedness strategies. In contrast, unvaccinated animals succumbed to infection. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 自 2024 年初以来,分支 2.3.4.4b 的 高致病性禽流感 A(H5N1) 病毒已在美国奶牛中引起广泛的 暴发,跨物种溢出 也感染到包括人类在内的哺乳动物物种。从人类病例中分离出的一种牛源性 A(H5N1) 病毒在哺乳动物模型中保留了高致病性和传播性,凸显了其大流行的潜力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项研究中,我们使用小鼠和雪貂模型评估了日本储存的基于 AS03 佐剂的 A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (H5N8) 分支 2.3.4.4b 流感 疫苗 的保护功效。接种疫苗和未接种疫苗的动物接受了与人类分离的牛 A(H5N1) 病毒基因相同的病毒的攻击。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究评估了中和抗体反应、器官中的病毒复制以及接种疫苗和未接种疫苗的动物模型的存活率。基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 储备 疫苗 已针对与牛 A(H5N1) 病毒的人类分离株基因相同的病毒进行了测试。
elements_zh.main_results: 疫苗接种 与基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 储备 疫苗 在两种动物模型中诱导强烈的中和抗体反应,显着抑制病毒复制,并提供针对致命挑战的完全保护。相比之下,所有未接种疫苗的小鼠和雪貂均死于感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 储备 疫苗 对牛 A(H5N1) 病毒具有强大的交叉保护功效。日本库存的基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 疫苗 可以在大流行的早期阶段作为针对牛 A(H5N1) 病毒的直接对策。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,储存的基于 A(H5N8) 的 疫苗 可以提供针对相关牛 A(H5N1) 病毒的保护,这可以为大流行防范策略提供信息。如果发生涉及 A(H5N1) 病毒的人畜共患 暴发,这可能会对大流行前 疫苗 的使用产生影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在动物模型中进行的,可能无法完全反映人类 免疫应答。证据充分证明 疫苗 对基因相同的牛 A(H5N1) 病毒具有保护功效,但对人类群体的普遍适用性仍不确定。

analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in animal models, which may not fully reflect human immune responses. The evidence is strong for the protective efficacy of the vaccine against genetically identical bovine A(H5N1) viruses, but generalisability to human populations remains uncertain.

papers.title_zh: A(H5N8) 储存的 疫苗 对与人类分离的牛 A(H5N1) 流感病毒基因相同的病毒的保护作用。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Since early 2024, highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses of clade 2.3.4.4b have caused extensive outbreaks in dairy cattle in the United States, with spillover into mammalian species, including humans. A bovine-derived A(H5N1) virus isolated from a human case retains high pathogenicity and transmissibility in mammalian models, highlighting its pandemic potential. Stockpiled pre-pandemic influenza vaccines are intended to provide early protection before strain-matched vaccines are available; however, their protective efficacy against bovine A(H5N1) viruses has not been directly evaluated in vivo. METHODS: In this study, we assessed the protective efficacy of an AS03-adjuvanted A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (H5N8) clade 2.3.4.4b-based influenza vaccine stockpiled in Japan using mouse and ferret models. Vaccinated and unvaccinated animals were challenged with a virus genetically identical to a human isolate of bovine A(H5N1) virus. Neutralising antibody responses, viral replication in organs, and survival were evaluated. FINDINGS: Vaccination with the AS03-adjuvanted A(H5N8)-based stockpiled vaccine induced robust neutralising antibody responses in both animal models, significantly suppressed viral replication, and conferred complete protection against lethal challenge. In contrast, all unvaccinated mice and ferrets succumbed to infection. These findings demonstrate that the AS03-adjuvanted A(H5N8)-based stockpiled vaccine provides strong cross-protective efficacy against bovine A(H5N1) viruses. INTERPRETATION: An AS03-adjuvanted A(H5N8)-based vaccine stockpiled in Japan could serve as an immediate countermeasure against bovine A(H5N1) viruses during the early phase of a pandemic. FUNDING: This work was supported by grants from the Japan Program for Infectious Diseases Research and Infrastructure (JP20wm0125002) and the Japan Initiative for World-leading Vaccine Research and Development Centers (JP223fa627001) from the Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:自 2024 年初以来,进化枝 2.3.4.4b 的 高致病性禽流感 A(H5N1) 病毒已在美国奶牛中引起广泛的 暴发 感染,跨物种溢出 感染包括人类在内的哺乳动物物种。从人类病例中分离出的一种牛源性 A(H5N1) 病毒在哺乳动物模型中保留了高致病性和传播性,凸显了其大流行的潜力。大流行前储存的流感 疫苗 旨在在毒株匹配的 疫苗 可用之前提供早期保护;然而,它们对牛 A(H5N1) 病毒的保护功效尚未在体内直接评估。方法:在本研究中,我们使用小鼠和雪貂模型评估了日本储存的基于 AS03 佐剂的 A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (H5N8) 分支 2.3.4.4b 流感 疫苗 的保护功效。接种疫苗和未接种疫苗的动物接受了与人类分离的牛 A(H5N1) 病毒基因相同的病毒的攻击。评估了中和抗体反应、器官中的病毒复制和存活率。结果:疫苗接种 与基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 储备 疫苗 在两种动物模型中诱导了强烈的中和抗体反应,显着抑制病毒复制,并提供针对致命攻击的完全保护。相比之下,所有未接种疫苗的小鼠和雪貂均死于感染。这些发现表明,基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 储备 疫苗 对牛 A(H5N1) 病毒具有强大的交叉保护功效。解读:日本储存的基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 疫苗 可以在大流行的早期阶段作为针对牛 A(H5N1) 病毒的直接对策。资助:这项工作得到了日本传染病研究和基础设施计划 (JP20wm0125002) 和日本医学研究与发展机构的日本世界领先 疫苗 研究与开发中心倡议 (JP223fa627001) 的资助。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 自 2024 年初以来,分支 2.3.4.4b 的 高致病性禽流感 A(H5N1) 病毒已在美国奶牛中引起广泛的 暴发,跨物种溢出 也感染到包括人类在内的哺乳动物物种。从人类病例中分离出的一种牛源性 A(H5N1) 病毒在哺乳动物模型中保留了高致病性和传播性,凸显了其大流行的潜力。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项研究中,我们使用小鼠和雪貂模型评估了日本储存的基于 AS03 佐剂的 A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (H5N8) 分支 2.3.4.4b 流感 疫苗 的保护功效。接种疫苗和未接种疫苗的动物接受了与人类分离的牛 A(H5N1) 病毒基因相同的病毒的攻击。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究评估了中和抗体反应、器官中的病毒复制以及接种疫苗和未接种疫苗的动物模型的存活率。基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 储备 疫苗 已针对与牛 A(H5N1) 病毒的人类分离株基因相同的病毒进行了测试。
analysis_zh.main_results: 疫苗接种 与基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 储备 疫苗 在两种动物模型中诱导强烈的中和抗体反应,显着抑制病毒复制,并提供针对致命挑战的完全保护。相比之下,所有未接种疫苗的小鼠和雪貂均死于感染。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 储备 疫苗 对牛 A(H5N1) 病毒具有强大的交叉保护功效。日本库存的基于 AS03 佐剂的 A(H5N8) 疫苗 可以在大流行的早期阶段作为针对牛 A(H5N1) 病毒的直接对策。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,储存的基于 A(H5N8) 的 疫苗 可以提供针对相关牛 A(H5N1) 病毒的保护,这可以为大流行防范策略提供信息。如果发生涉及 A(H5N1) 病毒的人畜共患 暴发,这可能会对大流行前 疫苗 的使用产生影响。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在动物模型中进行的,可能无法完全反映人类 免疫应答。证据充分证明 疫苗 对基因相同的牛 A(H5N1) 病毒具有保护功效,但对人类群体的普遍适用性仍不确定。

papers.title: Acquisition of specific human respiratory tract binding by 2.3.4.4b H5N1 hemagglutinins requires multiple mutations.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT It has been suggested that the hemagglutinin of the human-infecting cattle-derived 2.3.4.4b virus A/Texas/34 H5N1 (H5TX) requires only one mutation, namely Q226L, to switch from binding avian-type to human-type receptor preference. In this study, we examined the binding of H5TX Q226L, along with other key mutations, to sections of human trachea. We conclude that, while H5TX Q226L can bind human-type receptors, more than a single mutation is required for this protein to bind to human respiratory tract tissue. We also report changes in receptor-binding specificity of another 2.3.4.4b HA mutant, H5FR Q226L (from A/duck/France/161108/16 H5N8), associated with the presence of a multibasic cleavage site. This study offers insight into the determinants of evolution toward human-type receptor binding in currently circulating H5Nx viruses. It also emphasizes the importance of testing individual strains using additional methods, including tissue-based approaches, alongside synthetic glycans. IMPORTANCE Currently, H5N1 influenza A viruses are responsible for numerous zoonotic spillover events, from infecting birds to other mammals, including dairy cattle. Although no human-to-human transmission has been observed, several people have been infected. This host range expansion is typically linked to changes in one of the viral surface proteins, hemagglutinin, which can switch its preference from avian-type to human-type receptors. To better understand the potential of the currently circulating H5N1 virus to transmit among humans, we evaluated the effects of the Q226L mutation, in combination with other amino acid substitutions, on binding to the human trachea. We also studied the effect of the multibasic cleavage site, a specific motif present in highly pathogenic influenza strains, on receptor-binding properties. These findings provide insight into the role of receptor binding in influenza infections.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether the Q226L mutation in the hemagglutinin of the cattle-derived 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus (A/Texas/34) is sufficient to switch receptor binding from avian-type to human-type, a critical step for mammalian adaptation. Using human trachea tissue sections and synthetic glycans, the authors evaluated binding of H5TX Q226L and other hemagglutinin variants, including a multibasic cleavage site mutant from H5N8. They found that while Q226L enabled binding to human-type receptors, additional mutations were required for binding to human respiratory tract tissue. The study concludes that receptor binding to human tissue in 2.3.4.4b H5N1 requires more than a single mutation, underscoring the complexity of mammalian adaptation. These findings support the use of tissue-based assays alongside synthetic glycans in surveillance to better assess the pandemic potential of circulating H5Nx viruses.

Tuesday, August 11, 2026 Virology: Acquisition of specific human respiratory tract binding by 2.3.4.4b H5N1 hemagglutinins requires multiple mutations #19,288 There remains much interest in exactly what changes the HPAI H5Nx virus would need in order to become a more `humanized' virus - like seasonal H3N2 and H1N1 - which have a strong affinity for the alpha 2,6 receptor cells most commonly found in the human respiratory system. While it seems likely that it would require multiple concurrent mammalian adaptations to create a pandemic strain, the ability of avian flu viruses to bind to human α2-6 receptor cells is considered one of the biggest obstacles the virus must overcome in order to successfully spread in humans. Complicating matters, as we've discussed previously (see here, here, and here), HPAI H5 viruses encompass a large and growing array of closely related - but genetically distinct subclades, subtypes, and genotypes - and a mutation that might impact one strain might not have the same effect on another. In December of 2024, a study in Science: A Single Mutation in Bovine Influenza H5N1 Hemagglutinin Switches Specificity to Human Receptors, suggested a single HA amino acid change (Q226L) could switch H5N1 B3.13 from binding preferentially to avian-type receptor cells to human-type receptor cells. The authors wrote: “Our experiments revealed that the Q226L mutation could significantly increase the virus’ ability to target and attach to human-type receptors,” explains Paulson. “This mutation gives the virus a foothold on human cells that it didn’t have before, which is why this finding is a red flag for possible adaptation to people.” The shift alone, however, may not be enough to enable human-to-human transmission. Other genetic changes—such as mutations in polymerase basic 2 (E627K) that enhance viral replication and stability in human cells—would likely be necessary for the virus to spread efficiently among people. The following month, in Preprint: The Q226L Mutation Can Convert a Highly Pathogenic H5 2.3.4.4e Virus to Bind Human-type Receptors, another study (later published in PNAS) found that adding Q226L to an older clade 2.3.4.4e H5N6 virus could switch receptor binding from avian to human-type receptors. While concerning, we've not seen any evidence of efficient or sustained spread of H5N1 in humans, suggesting there are additional enhancements required. Today we've a new study that offers an update on impact of the Q226L mutation in H5N1 B3.13, which finds that its impact varies between HPAI H5 strains. While Q226L did shift binding in laboratory tests towards human-type glycans, those glycans were not found on the human tracheal tissues tested, and the Q226L mutant failed to bind human trachea. The addition of another HA mutation, N224K, increased human-tracheal binding, but only sparsely and mainly to goblet cells. All of which reinforces the notion that receptor adaptation to humans in HPAI H5 is neither simple nor uniform. Q226L appears to be decisive in some H5 strains, but the current bovine 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus likely requires additional changes before it can efficiently bind to human receptors in the upper airway. I've only posted the link, abstract, and some excerpts from the study. Follow the link to read it in its entirety. Guerreiro Cabana, Eszter Kovács, Zoé Ducarne, Cindy G. J. Cleypool , Geert-Jan Boons, Robert P. de Vries r.vries@uu.nlAuthors Info & Affiliations https://doi.org/10.1128/jvi.01065-26 ABSTRACT It has been suggested that the hemagglutinin of the human-infecting cattle-derived 2.3.4.4b virus A/Texas/34 H5N1 (H5TX) requires only one mutation, namely Q226L, to switch from binding avian-type to human-type receptor preference. In this study, we examined the binding of H5TX Q226L, along with other key mutations, to sections of human trachea. We conclude that, while H5TX Q226L can bind human-type receptors, more than a single mutation is required for this protein to bind to human respiratory tract tissue. We also report changes in receptor-binding specificity of another 2.3.4.4b HA mutant, H5FR Q226L (from A/duck/France/161108/16 H5N8), associated with the presence of a multibasic cleavage site. This study offers insight into the determinants of evolution toward human-type receptor binding in currently circulating H5Nx viruses. It also emphasizes the importance of testing individual strains using additional methods, including tissue-based approaches, alongside synthetic glycans. IMPORTANCE Currently, H5N1 influenza A viruses are responsible for numerous zoonotic spillover events, from infecting birds to other mammals, including dairy cattle. Although no human-to-human transmission has been observed, several people have been infected. This host range expansion is typically linked to changes in one of the viral surface proteins, hemagglutinin, which can switch its preference from avian-type to human-type receptors. To better understand the potential of the currently circulating H5N1 virus to transmit among humans, we evaluated the effects of the Q226L mutation, in combination with other amino acid substitutions, on binding to the human trachea. We also studied the effect of the multibasic cleavage site, a specific motif present in highly pathogenic influenza strains, on receptor-binding properties. These findings provide insight into the role of receptor binding in influenza infections. (SNIP) We conclude that more than a single mutation is required for the hemagglutinin of the currently circulating 2.3.4.4b viruses to bind human respiratory tissue. This aligns with previous work showing that multiple amino acid changes are required to switch from avian- to human-type receptors in H5 strains (3). One key takeaway from this study is the significance of glycan architecture. H5TX mutants, similarly to other HAs, distinguish not only between SIA linkage but are also selective according to glycan branch length and sialylation (31). More research is needed on the presence of asymmetrical glycans in the human respiratory tract and their role in influenza A virus hemagglutinin attachment to cells. Moreover, we emphasize the importance of not underestimating the MBCS’s influence on hemagglutinin’s receptor-binding properties. (Continue . . . ) Newer Post Older Post Home

papers.title: Risk assessment of avian influenza A(H5N5) virus from the first human case using the ferret model
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The incursion of Eurasian-origin genotype A6 A(H5N5) virus into North America expanded the genetic diversity among North American highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses and heightened concern about zoonotic risk. Following a fatal human infection with the A(H5N5) virus A/Washington/2148/2025, viral replication was assessed in polarized human bronchial epithelial cells, and pathogenicity, transmissibility in direct contact and respiratory droplet models, and airborne virus shedding were evaluated in ferrets to inform pandemic risk assessment. A(H5N5) displayed robust replication in Calu-3 cells at 33°C and 37°C, showing kinetics and peak titers comparable to those of contemporary genotype B3.13 and D1.1 A(H5N1) viruses. In ferrets, A(H5N5) replicated efficiently in the respiratory tract, disseminated to extrapulmonary tissues, and caused fatal disease in all inoculated animals. Airborne transmission was not observed, and infrequent, low-level detection of virus in air samples paralleled that of A(H5) viruses that are not transmissible via air in ferrets. In a direct contact model, limited transmission was detected within 4 days of exposure, with evidence of lower respiratory tract replication in contact animals. These findings indicate that the A(H5N5) virus has the capacity for robust replication in an airway epithelial cell line and can cause severe systemic infection and mortality in ferrets but has not acquired adaptations for airborne spread in mammals. Collectively, these results underscore heterogeneity among clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5Nx) viruses in North America and the need for genotype-by-genotype evaluation of newly emerged viruses to understand public health risk. IMPORTANCE The emergence of Eurasian-origin genotype A6 highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N5) virus in North America has increased viral diversity and raised concerns about zoonotic and pandemic risk. In this study, we evaluated the replication kinetics, pathogenesis, and transmission of A/Washington/2148/2025 A(H5N5) virus, which was isolated from the first reported human infection with this influenza virus subtype, using polarized human bronchial epithelial cells and the ferret model. The A(H5N5) virus replicated efficiently in vitro at temperatures representative of the upper and lower respiratory tracts and caused fatal systemic disease in inoculated ferrets. Limited transmission was observed during 4 days of direct contact. Airborne virus detection was infrequent and did not result in airborne transmission. These findings show that A(H5N5) virus can replicate robustly in mammalian cells and cause severe disease but lacks adaptations supporting efficient airborne spread, informing assessment of the pandemic risk posed by genotype A6 influenza viruses. Limited transmission was observed during 4 days of direct contact.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The emergence of Eurasian-origin genotype A6 A(H5N5) virus in North America increased viral diversity among highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses and raised concerns about zoonotic and pandemic risk, prompting a genotype-specific risk assessment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Following a fatal human infection with A(H5N5) virus A/Washington/2148/2025, the study assessed viral replication in polarized human bronchial epithelial cells and evaluated pathogenicity, transmissibility, and airborne virus shedding in ferrets.
analysis.methods: Viral replication was measured in Calu-3 cells at 33°C and 37°C, while ferrets were inoculated to assess replication in the respiratory tract, extrapulmonary dissemination, disease severity, and transmission via direct contact and respiratory droplet models.
analysis.main_results: A(H5N5) replicated efficiently in human bronchial epithelial cells and caused fatal systemic disease in all inoculated ferrets, with limited transmission detected in direct contact animals within 4 days and no airborne transmission observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that A(H5N5) can replicate robustly in mammalian cells and cause severe disease but lacks adaptations supporting efficient airborne spread in mammals, highlighting genotype-specific heterogeneity among clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5Nx) viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform pandemic risk assessment by demonstrating that genotype A6 A(H5N5) poses severe disease potential but currently lacks efficient mammalian transmission, underscoring the need for genotype-by-genotype evaluation of newly emerged viruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on the ferret model and short observation period for transmission, which may not fully capture human-relevant transmission dynamics or long-term risks, warranting cautious interpretation of the evidence strength as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the zoonotic risk of the Eurasian-origin genotype A6 A(H5N5) virus following a fatal human infection by assessing replication, pathogenesis, and transmission in human airway epithelial cells and ferrets. The A(H5N5) virus demonstrated robust replication in mammalian cells and caused fatal systemic disease in ferrets, with limited direct contact transmission but no airborne spread. These findings suggest that while A(H5N5) has severe disease potential, it currently lacks adaptations for efficient mammalian transmission, informing targeted risk assessments for clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5Nx) viruses.

papers.title_zh: 使用雪貂模型对首例人类病例中的 禽流感 A(H5N5) 病毒进行风险评估
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT The incursion of Eurasian-origin genotype A6 A(H5N5) virus into North America expanded the genetic diversity among North American highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses and heightened concern about zoonotic risk. Following a fatal human infection with the A(H5N5) virus A/Washington/2148/2025, viral replication was assessed in polarized human bronchial epithelial cells, and pathogenicity, transmissibility in direct contact and respiratory droplet models, and airborne virus shedding were evaluated in ferrets to inform pandemic risk assessment. A(H5N5) displayed robust replication in Calu-3 cells at 33°C and 37°C, showing kinetics and peak titers comparable to those of contemporary genotype B3.13 and D1.1 A(H5N1) viruses. In ferrets, A(H5N5) replicated efficiently in the respiratory tract, disseminated to extrapulmonary tissues, and caused fatal disease in all inoculated animals. Airborne transmission was not observed, and infrequent, low-level detection of virus in air samples paralleled that of A(H5) viruses that are not transmissible via air in ferrets. In a direct contact model, limited transmission was detected within 4 days of exposure, with evidence of lower respiratory tract replication in contact animals. These findings indicate that the A(H5N5) virus has the capacity for robust replication in an airway epithelial cell line and can cause severe systemic infection and mortality in ferrets but has not acquired adaptations for airborne spread in mammals. Collectively, these results underscore heterogeneity among clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5Nx) viruses in North America and the need for genotype-by-genotype evaluation of newly emerged viruses to understand public health risk. IMPORTANCE The emergence of Eurasian-origin genotype A6 highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N5) virus in North America has increased viral diversity and raised concerns about zoonotic and pandemic risk. In this study, we evaluated the replication kinetics, pathogenesis, and transmission of A/Washington/2148/2025 A(H5N5) virus, which was isolated from the first reported human infection with this influenza virus subtype, using polarized human bronchial epithelial cells and the ferret model. The A(H5N5) virus replicated efficiently in vitro at temperatures representative of the upper and lower respiratory tracts and caused fatal systemic disease in inoculated ferrets. Limited transmission was observed during 4 days of direct contact. Airborne virus detection was infrequent and did not result in airborne transmission. These findings show that A(H5N5) virus can replicate robustly in mammalian cells and cause severe disease but lacks adaptations supporting efficient airborne spread, informing assessment of the pandemic risk posed by genotype A6 influenza viruses. Limited transmission was observed during 4 days of direct contact.

papers.title: First detected incursions of avian influenza H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b into mainland Australia from the Southern Ocean
papers.abstract: Abstract High pathogenicity avian influenza H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has caused a panzootic of devastating impact to poultry and wildlife globally. The Australian continent and broader Oceania until recently remained the last major region without confirmed detections. Here we report the first H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b detections from two live seabirds - a brown skua and a southern giant petrel - found on the south coast of Western Australia in June 2026. Virus genome sequencing showed that both viruses were most closely related to H5N1 viruses detected recently on sub-Antarctic islands in the Southern Indian Ocean. In time-calibrated phylogeographic analyses, both viruses sampled in Western Australia clustered with viruses from Heard Island, a sub-Antarctic external territory of Australia. Ancestral location reconstruction also identified Heard Island as the most probable source location, although unsampled intermediate locations cannot be excluded. The two Western Australian detections were estimated to be independent incursions from Heard Island, rather than local transmission on mainland Australia. There was no evidence of reassortment with endemic avian influenza viruses in Australia, and both virus sequences retained key avian-like genetic markers and lacked known substitutions for reduced antiviral susceptibility. These detections revealed a Southern Ocean pathway of recurrent H5N1 incursions into Australia, highlighting the risk of potential establishment on the mainland and the need for heightened surveillance and rapid, nationally-coordinated, virus genomic characterisation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了尽管 高致病性禽流感 H5N1 进化枝 2.3.4.4b 在全球范围内传播的情况,但在澳大利亚大陆尚未确认检测到 高致病性禽流感 H5N1 进化枝 2.3.4.4b 的问题,旨在确定入侵该大陆的来源和途径。

elements_zh.main_results: 在西澳大利亚检测到的两种病毒与来自南印度洋亚南极岛屿的 H5N1 病毒关系最密切,系统发育地理学分析确定赫德岛是最有可能的来源地点。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调需要加强 监测 和快速、全国协调的病毒基因组表征,以监测和减轻 H5N1 在澳大利亚传播的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于赫德岛和澳大利亚大陆之间缺乏中间采样地点,证据受到限制,因此未采样的 传播 路线存在不确定性,而且该研究依赖于两次检测的小样本量。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 高致病性 禽流感 H5N1 分支 2.3.4.4b 已引起对全球家禽和野生动物造成毁灭性影响的大流行。直到最近,澳大利亚大陆和更广阔的大洋洲仍然是最后一个没有确认检测到的主要地区。在此,我们报告了 2026 年 6 月在西澳大利亚南海岸发现的两种活海鸟(棕色贼鸥和南方巨海燕)中首次检测到的 H5N1 分支 2.3.4.4b。病毒 基因组 测序表明,这两种病毒与最近在南印度洋亚南极岛屿上检测到的 H5N1 病毒关系最密切。在时间校准的系统发育地理学分析中,在西澳大利亚采样的两种病毒都与来自澳大利亚亚南极外部领土赫德岛的病毒聚集在一起。祖先位置重建也将赫德岛确定为最可能的源位置,尽管不能排除未采样的中间位置。西澳大利亚州的两次发现估计是来自赫德岛的独立入侵,而不是澳大利亚大陆当地的 传播。没有证据表明与澳大利亚地方性 禽流感 病毒重配,并且两种病毒序列都保留了关键的类禽遗传标记,并且缺乏已知的降低 抗病毒药物 易感性的替代。这些检测揭示了 H5N1 反复侵入澳大利亚的南大洋途径,凸显了在大陆潜在定居的风险,以及加强 监测 和快速、全国协调的病毒基因组特征分析的必要性。

papers.title: Beyond Entry: Evaluating the Internal Spread Risk of highly pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) H5N1 in Australia
papers.abstract: Abstract The highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus H5N1 is currently spreading worldwide, with Oceania remaining the only continent largely unaffected. However, recent detection of HPAI in wildlife on sub-Antarctic Heard Island highlights the increasing risk of incursion into mainland Australia. Migratory waterfowl and shorebirds, recognised as key vectors of avian influenza viruses (AIV), connect Australia with global transmission networks. Here, we developed an agent-based model to predict the spread of H5N1 following potential incursions across different regions of Australia. Our results suggest that the incursion region has a strong effect on outbreak spread and duration. The spread of H5N1 in Australia creates a substantial risk for poultry outbreaks and potential spillover into wildlife populations, particularly in ecologically sensitive breeding areas. These findings provide critical insights for informing national preparedness, guiding targeted surveillance, and strengthening One Health strategies to mitigate the impact of HPAI in Australia.
authors: Catarina do Carmo Norte dos Santos

source_records.abstract: Abstract The highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus H5N1 is currently spreading worldwide, with Oceania remaining the only continent largely unaffected. However, recent detection of HPAI in wildlife on sub-Antarctic Heard Island highlights the increasing risk of incursion into mainland Australia. Migratory waterfowl and shorebirds, recognised as key vectors of avian influenza viruses (AIV), connect Australia with global transmission networks. Here, we developed an agent-based model to predict the spread of H5N1 following potential incursions across different regions of Australia. Our results suggest that the incursion region has a strong effect on outbreak spread and duration. The spread of H5N1 in Australia creates a substantial risk for poultry outbreaks and potential spillover into wildlife populations, particularly in ecologically sensitive breeding areas. These findings provide critical insights for informing national preparedness, guiding targeted surveillance, and strengthening One Health strategies to mitigate the impact of HPAI in Australia.

papers.title: Genetic evolution, phylodynamics, geographic spread of H9N2 avian influenza viruses in China from 2014 to 2025: an increasing potential zoonotic risk.
papers.abstract: Subtype H9N2 of the avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a growing threat to the poultry industry and public health. However, since 2014, there has been no systematic study of its genetic evolution, genotype, spatial dynamics, and pathogenicity in China. Therefore, we performed a large-scale sequence analysis of the genome of Chinese H9N2 viruses from 2014 to 2025 using public databases and laboratory isolates. We identified 52 different genotypes in 1,591 H9N2 viruses, including 4 previously recognized genotypes (G6, G57, G58, and G68) and 48 newly defined genotypes (G118-G163) in this study. G57 and G118 were the main epidemic genotypes in China from 2014 to 2025. Bayesian phylogeographic analysis showed that there were 12 obvious migration paths for the spread of H9N2 AIVs in China from 2017 to 2022. In particular, the South China region was the main transmission centre. H9N2 AIV continues to circulate in chickens and ducks in China and spreads to other hosts. The H9N2 AIVs with the G57 and G118 genotypes could effectively replicate in MDCK, CEF, A549, and HBE cells with titres of 0.97-8.5 lgTCID50/mL. The G57 and G118 genotypes H9N2 viruses preferentially bound to α-2,6-linked sialic acid glycopolymers (human receptors), and effectively replicate in multiple organs of mice and chickens and cause pathological changes in the lungs. Thus, it is necessary to strengthen the monitoring and prevention of H9N2 AIVs in China.

papers.title_original: Genetic evolution, phylodynamics, geographic spread of H9N2 avian influenza viruses in China from 2014 to 2025: an increasing potential zoonotic risk.

analysis.research_question_and_background: H9N2 avian influenza virus (AIV) is an escalating threat to poultry and public health, yet prior to 2014 no systematic analysis had characterized its genetic evolution, genotype diversity, spatial spread, or pathogenicity in China.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a large-scale genomic sequence analysis of H9N2 AIVs circulating in China from 2014 to 2025 using public databases and laboratory isolates.
analysis.methods: Genome sequences were retrieved and analyzed to define genotypes and perform Bayesian phylogeographic reconstruction of viral migration patterns across Chinese regions from 2017 to 2022.
analysis.main_results: A total of 52 genotypes were identified among 1,591 H9N2 viruses, including 48 newly defined genotypes (G118–G163), with G57 and G118 emerging as the dominant epidemic genotypes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the rapid diversification and geographic expansion of H9N2 genotypes as evidence of increasing zoonotic potential, highlighting G57 and G118 as genotypes of particular concern.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support enhanced surveillance and prevention strategies for H9N2 AIV in China to mitigate poultry losses and reduce zoonotic spillover risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on publicly available sequences and laboratory isolates, which may underrepresent geographic and temporal diversity, limiting generalizability and introducing sampling bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed 1,591 H9N2 avian influenza virus genomes from China spanning 2014 to 2025 to assess genetic evolution, genotype diversity, and geographic spread. The authors identified 52 genotypes, including 48 newly defined ones, with G57 and G118 dominating circulation. Bayesian phylogeographic analysis revealed 12 migration pathways across China from 2017 to 2022, with South China identified as a major transmission hub. The study highlights the increasing zoonotic potential of H9N2, particularly for genotypes G57 and G118, which showed efficient replication in mammalian and avian cells and preferential binding to human-type receptors. The findings underscore the need for strengthened monitoring and prevention measures to address the growing threat posed by H9N2 to poultry and public health.

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the rapid diversification and geographic expansion of H9N2 genotypes as evidence of increasing zoonotic potential, highlighting G57 and G118 as genotypes of particular concern.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support enhanced surveillance and prevention strategies for H9N2 AIV in China to mitigate poultry losses and reduce zoonotic spillover risk.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on publicly available sequences and laboratory isolates, which may underrepresent geographic and temporal diversity, limiting generalizability and introducing sampling bias.

papers.title_zh: 2014年至2025年中国H9N2 进化病毒的基因进化、系统动力学、地理传播:潜在人畜共患病风险不断增加。
papers.source_body_en: Subtype H9N2 of the avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a growing threat to the poultry industry and public health. However, since 2014, there has been no systematic study of its genetic evolution, genotype, spatial dynamics, and pathogenicity in China. Therefore, we performed a large-scale sequence analysis of the genome of Chinese H9N2 viruses from 2014 to 2025 using public databases and laboratory isolates. We identified 52 different genotypes in 1,591 H9N2 viruses, including 4 previously recognized genotypes (G6, G57, G58, and G68) and 48 newly defined genotypes (G118-G163) in this study. G57 and G118 were the main epidemic genotypes in China from 2014 to 2025. Bayesian phylogeographic analysis showed that there were 12 obvious migration paths for the spread of H9N2 AIVs in China from 2017 to 2022. In particular, the South China region was the main transmission centre. H9N2 AIV continues to circulate in chickens and ducks in China and spreads to other hosts. The H9N2 AIVs with the G57 and G118 genotypes could effectively replicate in MDCK, CEF, A549, and HBE cells with titres of 0.97-8.5 lgTCID50/mL. The G57 and G118 genotypes H9N2 viruses preferentially bound to α-2,6-linked sialic acid glycopolymers (human receptors), and effectively replicate in multiple organs of mice and chickens and cause pathological changes in the lungs. Thus, it is necessary to strengthen the monitoring and prevention of H9N2 AIVs in China.

papers.title: Livestock production intensity and mucosal IgA and IgG responses to H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza A virus, North Carolina, 2021-2022
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Direct livestock exposure is a risk factor for zoonotic influenza, including H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A virus. But whether living in regions of high poultry and swine production intensity (PPI, SPI) increases risk of exposure to zoonotic influenza viruses independent of occupational livestock contact remains unclear. Objectives To determine whether livestock workers and community members with no occupational livestock exposure in North Carolina, where poultry and swine production are increasingly co-located, are at higher risk of exposure to zoonotic influenza. Methods Saliva samples from industrial livestock operation worker (ILO-W), ILO neighbor (ILO-N) and metropolitan area (Metro) households were analyzed for mucosal influenza A (H5N1, H1N1, and H3N2) hemagglutinin (HA) IgA and IgG antibodies to determine associations of PPI, SPI, exposure group, and detection of a swine-specific fecal contamination marker (Pig-2-Bac DNA) with influenza A antibody levels. Results Residing in the highest PPI and SPI tertile was associated with significantly higher mucosal H5 and H1 HA IgA levels, including among residents without occupational livestock exposure. Households with occupational poultry or swine contact had significantly higher H5 IgA and IgG and H1 IgA levels compared to Metro households. In regression models accounting for clustering at the participant level, log 10 anti-H5 HA mucosal IgA increased 0.16 (95% CI: 0.06, 0.27, p <0.005) and 0.10 (95% CI: 0.03, 0.17, p <0.005), per log 10 increase in PPI and SPI, respectively, and 0.16 (95% CI: 0.03, 0.19, p <0.02) when Pig-2-Bac DNA was detected on household surfaces. Conclusions Mucosal H5 HA IgA and IgG and H1 HA IgA were consistently elevated across different metrics of livestock exposure intensity, including residential exposure, occupational contact within a household, and a molecular marker of household swine fecal contamination in a state with intensive poultry and swine production.

However, it remains unclear whether living in regions with high poultry and swine production intensity increases exposure risk independent of occupational contact.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study collected saliva samples from industrial livestock operation workers (ILO-W), their neighbors (ILO-N), and metropolitan area households (Metro) in North Carolina during 2021–2022 to assess mucosal influenza A antibody responses.
analysis.methods: Saliva samples were analyzed for mucosal influenza A hemagglutinin (HA) IgA and IgG antibodies against H5N1, H1N1, and H3N2, and associations were examined with poultry production intensity (PPI), swine production intensity (SPI), exposure group, and a swine-specific fecal contamination marker (Pig-2-Bac DNA) using regression models accounting for participant-level clustering.
analysis.main_results: Residing in the highest PPI and SPI tertiles was associated with significantly higher mucosal H5 and H1 HA IgA levels, including among residents without occupational livestock exposure. Households with occupational poultry or swine contact had significantly higher H5 IgA and IgG and H1 IgA levels than Metro households.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that residential exposure to intensive livestock production and molecular markers of swine fecal contamination are associated with elevated mucosal antibodies to H5 and H1 influenza A viruses, highlighting a potential pathway for zoonotic exposure beyond occupational contact.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that surveillance and prevention strategies for H5N1 HPAI should consider residential proximity to high-density poultry and swine operations and environmental contamination as risk factors, even among non-occupationally exposed community members.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which precludes causal inference, and reliance on antibody detection rather than direct virus detection, potentially reflecting past exposure rather than current infection risk. The evidence strength is moderate given the robust sampling and statistical adjustment but constrained by design limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether living in regions with high poultry and swine production intensity (PPI, SPI) increases exposure risk to zoonotic influenza A viruses, including H5N1 HPAI, independent of occupational livestock contact. Saliva samples from industrial livestock workers, their neighbors, and metropolitan households in North Carolina (2021–2022) were analyzed for mucosal antibodies to H5, H1, and H3 influenza A viruses. Residing in the highest PPI and SPI tertiles was associated with significantly higher mucosal H5 and H1 HA IgA levels, including among non-occupationally exposed residents. Households with occupational poultry or swine contact showed higher H5 IgA and IgG and H1 IgA levels than metropolitan households. Regression models indicated that log-transformed anti-H5 HA mucosal IgA increased by 0.16 per log10 PPI and 0.10 per log10 SPI, with an additional increase when Pig-2-Bac DNA was detected. The authors conclude that residential exposure to intensive livestock production and environmental swine fecal contamination are associated with elevated mucosal antibodies to H5 and H1 influenza A viruses, suggesting a potential pathway for zoonotic exposure beyond occupational contact.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人畜共患流感会带来公共卫生风险,直接接触牲畜是 H5N1 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) A 病毒感染的已知危险因素。然而,目前尚不清楚生活在家禽和生猪生产强度较高的地区是否会增加暴露风险,而与职业接触无关。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究收集了 2021 年至 2022 年北卡罗来纳州工业畜牧业工人 (ILO-W)、其邻居 (ILO-N) 和大都市区家庭 (Metro) 的唾液样本,以评估粘膜甲型流感抗体反应。
elements_zh.methods: 分析唾液样本中针对 H5N1、H1N1 和 H3N2 的粘膜甲型流感血凝素 (HA) IgA 和 IgG 抗体,并使用考虑参与者水平聚类的回归模型检查与家禽生产强度 (PPI)、猪生产强度 (SPI)、暴露组和猪特异性粪便污染标记 (Pig-2-Bac DNA) 之间的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 居住在最高 PPI 和 SPI 三分位的人与显着较高的粘膜 H5 和 H1 HA IgA 水平相关,包括在没有职业性牲畜接触的居民中。职业性接触家禽或猪的家庭的 H5 IgA 和 IgG 以及 H1 IgA 水平显着高于都市家庭。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,证明居住地接触集约化畜牧生产和猪粪便污染的分子标记物与 H5 和 H1 甲型流感病毒粘膜抗体升高有关,这突显了职业接触之外的人畜共患接触的潜在途径。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些研究结果表明,监测 和 H5N1 HPAI 预防策略应将居住地邻近高密度家禽和猪养殖场以及环境污染视为风险因素,即使是在非职业暴露的社区成员中也是如此。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横断面设计的限制,排除了因果推断,并且依赖抗体检测而不是直接病毒检测,可能反映了过去的暴露而不是当前的感染风险。考虑到稳健的抽样和统计调整,证据强度中等,但受到设计限制。

papers.title_zh: 2021-2022 年北卡罗来纳州牲畜生产强度以及对 H5N1 高致病性禽流感 A 病毒的粘膜 IgA 和 IgG 反应
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Direct livestock exposure is a risk factor for zoonotic influenza, including H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A virus. But whether living in regions of high poultry and swine production intensity (PPI, SPI) increases risk of exposure to zoonotic influenza viruses independent of occupational livestock contact remains unclear. Objectives To determine whether livestock workers and community members with no occupational livestock exposure in North Carolina, where poultry and swine production are increasingly co-located, are at higher risk of exposure to zoonotic influenza. Methods Saliva samples from industrial livestock operation worker (ILO-W), ILO neighbor (ILO-N) and metropolitan area (Metro) households were analyzed for mucosal influenza A (H5N1, H1N1, and H3N2) hemagglutinin (HA) IgA and IgG antibodies to determine associations of PPI, SPI, exposure group, and detection of a swine-specific fecal contamination marker (Pig-2-Bac DNA) with influenza A antibody levels. Results Residing in the highest PPI and SPI tertile was associated with significantly higher mucosal H5 and H1 HA IgA levels, including among residents without occupational livestock exposure. Households with occupational poultry or swine contact had significantly higher H5 IgA and IgG and H1 IgA levels compared to Metro households. In regression models accounting for clustering at the participant level, log 10 anti-H5 HA mucosal IgA increased 0.16 (95% CI: 0.06, 0.27, p <0.005) and 0.10 (95% CI: 0.03, 0.17, p <0.005), per log 10 increase in PPI and SPI, respectively, and 0.16 (95% CI: 0.03, 0.19, p <0.02) when Pig-2-Bac DNA was detected on household surfaces. Conclusions Mucosal H5 HA IgA and IgG and H1 HA IgA were consistently elevated across different metrics of livestock exposure intensity, including residential exposure, occupational contact within a household, and a molecular marker of household swine fecal contamination in a state with intensive poultry and swine production.

papers.title: Molecular Surveillance and Nanopore Sequencing Reveal the Circulation and Genetic Diversity of Low-Pathogenic Avian Influenza A Viruses in Migratory Birds from Ukraine
papers.abstract: Wild migratory birds are the principal natural reservoir of influenza A viruses (IAVs) and play a central role in their evolution and global dissemination. Ukraine lies along the Black Sea–Mediterranean Flyway, making surveillance of avian influenza viruses in wild birds essential within a One Health framework, although genomic data from the region remain limited. Between October 2025 and January 2026 In some places you say December 2025 and in other places you say January 2026. I do not understand the differences, 604 cloacal and oropharyngeal swabs and environmental fecal samples were collected from migratory birds and mixed-species flocks in the Tuzlivski lymany National Nature Park and surrounding areas, together with samples from nearby domestic poultry. Influenza A virus was detected by real-time RT-PCR targeting the matrix gene, followed by H5/H7 screening, Oxford Nanopore sequencing of complete hemagglutinin genes, and phylogenetic analysis. Influenza A virus RNA was identified in 30/604 samples (4.97%), whereas all samples were negative for H5 and H7 subtypes. Complete hemagglutinin sequences revealed three low-pathogenic subtypes (H1, H4, and H6) that clustered within established Eurasian lineages closely related to contemporary avian viruses circulating across Europe, Asia, and North America. No influenza A virus or Newcastle disease virus was detected in domestic poultry. These findings provide an important genomic baseline for avian influenza surveillance in Ukraine and demonstrate the value of portable nanopore sequencing and integrated One Health surveillance for monitoring viral diversity and supporting early detection of emerging influenza threats.

papers.title: Revolutionising notifiable avian disease diagnostics: validation of direct swab testing for Avian Influenza and Newcastle disease using the CENOS platform
papers.abstract: Existing molecular diagnostic approaches for notifiable avian diseases (NADs) involve a suite of PCR assays that enable both generic detection, and where positive, subtyping of both avian influenza virus (AIV) and Newcastle disease virus (NDV). Novel rapid and direct diagnostic assays for the detection of AIV and NDV were developed and evaluated using unprocessed cloacal (C) and oropharyngeal (OP) poultry swab material. Both assays employ a closed tube direct real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RRT PCR) approach in which viral lysis is achieved by heat treatment and a dedicated PCR compatible buffer, followed by detection using a RRT-PCR approach. Primer and probe sets were designed using globally circulating AIV and NDV sequences collected over the preceding five years, rather than region specific sequence datasets, so that the assays detect all circulating genotypes. Analytical performance assessment demonstrated that both assays were highly sensitive and specific, successfully detecting all unextracted target antigens without cross reactivity to a panel of other common poultry pathogens. For each assay, viral lysis and amplification were achieved directly from samples at single digit genome copy numbers. Furthermore, low levels of viral RNA could be reliably detected in the presence of C and OP matrix material, providing proof of concept for direct detection of these economically significant avian pathogens in a field setting. Additional use case scenarios, including pooled sample screening and combined C/OP testing from individual birds, were also explored. These findings establish a foundation for ongoing studies incorporating paired sample testing against validated laboratory reference assays.

papers.title_zh: 彻底改变应通报的禽类疾病诊断:使用 CENOS 平台验证 禽流感 和新城疫的直接拭子检测
papers.source_body_en: Existing molecular diagnostic approaches for notifiable avian diseases (NADs) involve a suite of PCR assays that enable both generic detection, and where positive, subtyping of both avian influenza virus (AIV) and Newcastle disease virus (NDV). Novel rapid and direct diagnostic assays for the detection of AIV and NDV were developed and evaluated using unprocessed cloacal (C) and oropharyngeal (OP) poultry swab material. Both assays employ a closed tube direct real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RRT PCR) approach in which viral lysis is achieved by heat treatment and a dedicated PCR compatible buffer, followed by detection using a RRT-PCR approach. Primer and probe sets were designed using globally circulating AIV and NDV sequences collected over the preceding five years, rather than region specific sequence datasets, so that the assays detect all circulating genotypes. Analytical performance assessment demonstrated that both assays were highly sensitive and specific, successfully detecting all unextracted target antigens without cross reactivity to a panel of other common poultry pathogens. For each assay, viral lysis and amplification were achieved directly from samples at single digit genome copy numbers. Furthermore, low levels of viral RNA could be reliably detected in the presence of C and OP matrix material, providing proof of concept for direct detection of these economically significant avian pathogens in a field setting. Additional use case scenarios, including pooled sample screening and combined C/OP testing from individual birds, were also explored. These findings establish a foundation for ongoing studies incorporating paired sample testing against validated laboratory reference assays.

papers.title: Development of a multi-species luciferase-based double-antigen ELISA for the detection of antibodies against influenza A virus H5 clade 2.3.4.4b.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: The highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses of subtype H5N1 represent a major threat to animal and public health. The current panzootic with H5 clade 2.3.4.4b has caused numerous, widespread outbreaks in various domestic and wild avian species with high mortalities, massive losses, and a high frequency of spillover events to unexpected novel mammalian hosts, such as dairy cows. The global H5N1 situation raises serious concerns about zoonotic risks due to effective mammal-to-mammal transmission. Therefore, it is critical to increase surveillance intensity of a broadened species range, particularly at the human-animal interface. For this purpose, reliable and cost-effective serological tools that are easy to perform and suitable for high-throughput screening are critically needed. The newly developed double-antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay format employing a luminescence-based detection technology has demonstrated compliance with such prerequisites. The assay allowed sensitive and specific detection of antibodies directed against H5 hemagglutinin of clade 2.3.4.4b in a wide range of birds and mammals, including humans. Furthermore, it allowed differentiating H5 anti-head-specific from cross-reacting anti-stalk antibodies, which represents a valuable feature with regard to the monitoring of future vaccination programs with H5-specific vaccines. Thus, the assay is a significant contribution to existing serological diagnostic tests for a clade-optimized and species-independent detection of influenza A virus antibodies. IMPORTANCE: The ongoing highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1 panzootic has caused numerous outbreaks in domestic and wild animals, with frequent spillover events to unexpected host species, which underscores the importance of intensified surveillance. However, sensitive and specific multi-species serological assays represent a major gap. For this purpose, we developed a novel double-antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay that employs an innovative luminescence-based readout strategy. The test allowed a highly sensitive and specific detection of H5-specific antibodies in a wide range of avian and mammalian species, including humans. It therefore represents a valuable contribution to improving species-independent serological diagnostic tools for the detection of influenza A virus antibodies.

papers.title_zh: 开发基于多物种荧光素酶的双抗原 ELISA,用于检测甲型流感病毒 H5 进化枝 2.3.4.4b 的抗体。
papers.source_body_en: UNLABELLED: The highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses of subtype H5N1 represent a major threat to animal and public health. The current panzootic with H5 clade 2.3.4.4b has caused numerous, widespread outbreaks in various domestic and wild avian species with high mortalities, massive losses, and a high frequency of spillover events to unexpected novel mammalian hosts, such as dairy cows. The global H5N1 situation raises serious concerns about zoonotic risks due to effective mammal-to-mammal transmission. Therefore, it is critical to increase surveillance intensity of a broadened species range, particularly at the human-animal interface. For this purpose, reliable and cost-effective serological tools that are easy to perform and suitable for high-throughput screening are critically needed. The newly developed double-antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay format employing a luminescence-based detection technology has demonstrated compliance with such prerequisites. The assay allowed sensitive and specific detection of antibodies directed against H5 hemagglutinin of clade 2.3.4.4b in a wide range of birds and mammals, including humans. Furthermore, it allowed differentiating H5 anti-head-specific from cross-reacting anti-stalk antibodies, which represents a valuable feature with regard to the monitoring of future vaccination programs with H5-specific vaccines. Thus, the assay is a significant contribution to existing serological diagnostic tests for a clade-optimized and species-independent detection of influenza A virus antibodies. IMPORTANCE: The ongoing highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1 panzootic has caused numerous outbreaks in domestic and wild animals, with frequent spillover events to unexpected host species, which underscores the importance of intensified surveillance. However, sensitive and specific multi-species serological assays represent a major gap. For this purpose, we developed a novel double-antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay that employs an innovative luminescence-based readout strategy. The test allowed a highly sensitive and specific detection of H5-specific antibodies in a wide range of avian and mammalian species, including humans. It therefore represents a valuable contribution to improving species-independent serological diagnostic tools for the detection of influenza A virus antibodies.

papers.title: A cross-sectional study of avian influenza virus in poultry markets of Guangdong China, 2025
papers.abstract: Background Guangdong, China is a critical epicenter for avian influenza virus (AIV) emergence, where H5N1 and highly pathogenic H7N9 were first identified. Monitoring AIV genotype distribution and genetic diversity in this region is essential for providing early warnings and mitigating the risk of human infections. Methods In May 2025, a cross-sectional study was conducted across 4 representative cities in Guangdong. We collected 500 environmental swabs and 45 wastewater samples from 23 live poultry markets (LPMs). Samples were screened for influenza A virus (IAV) and subtyped for H5, H7, and H9. Next generation sequencing (NGS) and phylogenetic analyses were employed to characterize viral diversity and zoonotic potential. Results AIV was detected in 49.2% (246/500) of environmental samples. H9 was the dominant subtype (38.2%), followed by H5 (3.2%) and H7 (0.8%); 2.4% of positive samples showed multi-subtype co-occurrence. “Non-restricted zone” markets (80.0%) and “waste storage areas” (68.4%) were identified as primary contamination hotspots. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that H5 and H9 viruses are accumulating mutations linked to enhanced human-type receptor affinity. Notably, H5 and H6 sequences exhibited long internal branches and clustered with isolates from other Asian countries rather than domestic strains, highlighting a significant gap in current domestic molecular surveillance and a lack of continuous evolutionary data for these genotypes. Conclusions Widespread AIV contamination persists in Guangdong LPMs, dominated by H9 with low-level circulation of highly pathogenic subtypes. The identified surveillance gaps for H5/H6 and the presence of multi-subtype environments underscore the urgent need for strengthened, integrated molecular monitoring and stricter market regulation to mitigate public health risks.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 中国广东省是 禽流感 病毒 (AIV) 出现的关键震中,H5N1 和高致病性 H7N9 都是在该地区首次发现的。监测该地区 AIV 基因型分布和遗传多样性对于提供早期预警和减轻人类感染风险至关重要。方法 2025年5月,对广东省4个代表性城市进行横断面研究。我们从 23 个活禽市场 (LPM) 收集了 500 个环境拭子和 45 个废水样本。对样本进行甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 筛查并进行 H5、H7 和 H9 亚型分析。采用下一代测序(NGS)和系统发育分析来表征病毒多样性和人畜共患潜力。结果 49.2% (246/500) 的环境样本中检测到 AIV。H9 是主要亚型(38.2%),其次是 H5(3.2%)和 H7(0.8%);2.4%的阳性样本表现出多亚型共现。“非限制区”市场(80.0%)和“垃圾存放区”(68.4%)被确定为主要污染热点地区。系统发育分析显示,H5 和 H9 病毒正在积累与增强的人型受体亲和力相关的 突变。值得注意的是,H5和H6序列表现出较长的内部分支,并与来自其他亚洲国家而不是国内菌株的分离株聚集在一起,突显了当前国内分子监测的显着差距以及这些基因型缺乏连续进化数据。结论 广东省低病毒感染地区持续存在广泛的禽流感病毒污染,以H9为主,高致病性亚型的低水平循环。已确定的 H5/H6 的 监测 差距和多亚型环境的存在强调了迫切需要加强、综合分子监测和更严格的市场监管,以减轻公共卫生风险。

analysis_zh.main_results: 49.2% (246/500) 的环境样本中检测到 AIV,其中 H9 为主要亚型 (38.2%),其次是 H5 (3.2%) 和 H7 (0.8%);2.4%的阳性样本表现出多亚型共现。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 系统发育分析表明,H5和H9病毒正在积累与增强的人型受体亲和力相关的突变,揭示了国内分子监测和H5/H6基因型的连续进化数据的差距。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果突显了以H9为主的活禽市场持续存在禽流感病毒污染,高致病性亚型的低水平流通,强调需要加强分子监测和更严格的市场监管,以减轻公共卫生风险。

papers.title: Molecular epidemiological characteristics of H9N2 subtype avian influenza virus in the external environment of western Zhejiang, China, 2014–2025
papers.abstract: Objective To elucidate the epidemiological distribution patterns of avian influenza virus (AIV) in the external environment of western Zhejiang from 2014 to 2025, analyze the molecular epidemiological characteristics of the H9N2 subtype, and assess its public health risks. Methods According to the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Program for Avian Influenza in Occupationally Exposed Populations and External Environments, real-time RT-PCR was used to detect AIV subtypes in environmental specimens. H9N2-positive samples with cycle threshold values <30 were inoculated into specific pathogen-free (SPF) embryonated chicken eggs for virus isolation, followed by whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis for phylogenetic and molecular characterization. Results A total of 7,762 specimens were tested from 2014 to 2025, with an overall positivity rate of 34.64% (2,689/7,762) for AIV. Significant differences in positivity rates were observed in seasons, regions, sampling sites, and specimen types (all p < 0.001). AIV activity peaked in winter and spring, with the highest rates detected in live poultry markets and chopping board swabs. The H9 was the predominant subtype, with co-circulation of multiple subtypes. All 48 H9N2 subtype isolates belonged to the G57 genotype, with the hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) genes falling into the Y280-like branch, while the internal genes exhibited a mosaic pattern combining G1-like and F/98-like lineages. Molecular characterization analysis revealed multiple mammalian adaptive mutations, involving alterations in receptor-binding sites (T163N, H191N, T197D, T198V, Q234L, Q235M), antigenic epitopes (D280G, N285S), and glycosylation sites (218NRTF, 313NCSK). NA stalk deletion (62–64 aa), along with multiple mutations in the hemadsorption site (E/K368N, D369S/G, D401G/V, N402D, W403L/R, Q432H). Additionally, multiple key amino acid substitutions were also identified in the internal proteins. Conclusion The external environment in western Zhejiang exhibits a high prevalence of AIVs with pronounced spatiotemporal clustering. H9 was the dominant subtype and co-circulated with multiple subtypes, with live poultry markets and slaughterhouses identified as high-risk settings. The H9N2 subtype AIV has accumulated multiple mammalian adaptive mutations, and exhibits genetic linkages across eastern Chinese provinces. These findings collectively underscore the need for an integrated One Health surveillance and early-warning system to reduce the risk of human infections with avian influenza.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health need to characterize environmental circulation of avian influenza viruses (AIVs) in western Zhejiang, China, where subtype diversity and zoonotic risk remain insufficiently understood. It aimed to map AIV distribution patterns, define the molecular epidemiology of the H9N2 subtype, and evaluate associated public-health risks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A longitudinal environmental surveillance study was conducted from 2014 to 2025 in western Zhejiang, China, under the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Program for Avian Influenza in Occupationally Exposed Populations and External Environments. A total of 7,762 environmental specimens were collected and tested for AIV.
analysis.methods: Real-time RT-PCR was used to detect AIV subtypes in environmental specimens. H9N2-positive samples with cycle threshold values below 30 were inoculated into specific pathogen-free embryonated chicken eggs for virus isolation, followed by whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis for phylogenetic and molecular characterization.
analysis.main_results: Of 7,762 specimens, 2,689 (34.64%) tested positive for AIV. Positivity rates differed significantly by season, region, sampling site, and specimen type (all p < 0.001). AIV activity peaked in winter and spring, with the highest rates in live poultry markets and chopping board swabs. All 48 H9N2 isolates belonged to the G57 genotype, with HA and NA genes clustering in the Y280-like branch and internal genes showing a mosaic pattern of G1-like and F/98-like lineages.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the sustained high prevalence and spatiotemporal clustering as evidence of persistent environmental circulation of H9N2 in western Zhejiang, with live poultry markets acting as major reservoirs. They highlight the accumulation of mammalian adaptive mutations and genetic linkages across eastern China as novel indicators of potential zoonotic risk.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted environmental surveillance and risk-based interventions in high-risk settings such as live poultry markets and slaughterhouses to reduce spillover risk. They also justify strengthening One Health coordination for early warning and outbreak preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s reliance on environmental sampling may underrepresent human exposure pathways and lacks direct evidence of human infection. Despite robust phylogenetic and molecular analyses, the absence of experimental transmission or pathogenesis data limits causal inference; overall evidence strength is assessed as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This longitudinal environmental surveillance study in western Zhejiang, China (2014–2025) tested 7,762 specimens and found a 34.64% overall avian influenza virus (AIV) positivity rate, with significant spatiotemporal variation and peaks in winter and spring. H9N2 was the predominant subtype, and all 48 H9N2 isolates belonged to the G57 genotype, showing Y280-like hemagglutinin and neuraminidase genes and mosaic internal genes. Molecular characterization revealed multiple mammalian adaptive mutations in receptor-binding, antigenic epitopes, and glycosylation sites, alongside a 62–64 amino acid neuraminidase stalk deletion. The authors conclude that live poultry markets and slaughterhouses are high-risk settings and call for integrated One Health surveillance to mitigate zoonotic risk.

It aimed to map AIV distribution patterns, define the molecular epidemiology of the H9N2 subtype, and evaluate associated public-health risks.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A longitudinal environmental surveillance study was conducted from 2014 to 2025 in western Zhejiang, China, under the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Program for Avian Influenza in Occupationally Exposed Populations and External Environments. A total of 7,762 environmental specimens were collected and tested for AIV.
analysis_en.methods: Real-time RT-PCR was used to detect AIV subtypes in environmental specimens. H9N2-positive samples with cycle threshold values below 30 were inoculated into specific pathogen-free embryonated chicken eggs for virus isolation, followed by whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis for phylogenetic and molecular characterization.

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the sustained high prevalence and spatiotemporal clustering as evidence of persistent environmental circulation of H9N2 in western Zhejiang, with live poultry markets acting as major reservoirs. papers.title_zh: 2014-2025年浙江西部外部环境H9N2亚型禽流感病毒分子流行病学特征
papers.source_body_en: Objective To elucidate the epidemiological distribution patterns of avian influenza virus (AIV) in the external environment of western Zhejiang from 2014 to 2025, analyze the molecular epidemiological characteristics of the H9N2 subtype, and assess its public health risks. Methods According to the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Program for Avian Influenza in Occupationally Exposed Populations and External Environments, real-time RT-PCR was used to detect AIV subtypes in environmental specimens. H9N2-positive samples with cycle threshold values <30 were inoculated into specific pathogen-free (SPF) embryonated chicken eggs for virus isolation, followed by whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis for phylogenetic and molecular characterization. Results A total of 7,762 specimens were tested from 2014 to 2025, with an overall positivity rate of 34.64% (2,689/7,762) for AIV. Significant differences in positivity rates were observed in seasons, regions, sampling sites, and specimen types (all p < 0.001). AIV activity peaked in winter and spring, with the highest rates detected in live poultry markets and chopping board swabs. The H9 was the predominant subtype, with co-circulation of multiple subtypes. All 48 H9N2 subtype isolates belonged to the G57 genotype, with the hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) genes falling into the Y280-like branch, while the internal genes exhibited a mosaic pattern combining G1-like and F/98-like lineages. Molecular characterization analysis revealed multiple mammalian adaptive mutations, involving alterations in receptor-binding sites (T163N, H191N, T197D, T198V, Q234L, Q235M), antigenic epitopes (D280G, N285S), and glycosylation sites (218NRTF, 313NCSK). NA stalk deletion (62–64 aa), along with multiple mutations in the hemadsorption site (E/K368N, D369S/G, D401G/V, N402D, W403L/R, Q432H). Additionally, multiple key amino acid substitutions were also identified in the internal proteins. Conclusion The external environment in western Zhejiang exhibits a high prevalence of AIVs with pronounced spatiotemporal clustering. H9 was the dominant subtype and co-circulated with multiple subtypes, with live poultry markets and slaughterhouses identified as high-risk settings. The H9N2 subtype AIV has accumulated multiple mammalian adaptive mutations, and exhibits genetic linkages across eastern Chinese provinces. These findings collectively underscore the need for an integrated One Health surveillance and early-warning system to reduce the risk of human infections with avian influenza.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的 揭示2014—2025年浙西地区外部环境禽流感病毒(AIV)流行病学分布规律,分析H9N2亚型分子流行病学特征,评估其公共卫生风险。方法根据浙江省职业暴露人群及外部环境禽流感规划,采用实时荧光定量RT-PCR技术检测环境标本中AIV亚型。将循环阈值<30的H9N2阳性样本接种到无特定病原体(SPF)的含胚鸡蛋中进行病毒分离,然后进行全基因组测序和生物信息学分析以进行系统发育和分子表征。结果 2014年至2025年共检测标本7,762份,AIV总体阳性率为34.64%(2,689/7,762)。季节、地区、采样地点和标本类型之间的阳性率存在显着差异(所有 p < 0.001)。禽流感病毒活动在冬季和春季达到高峰,活禽市场和案板拭子中检测到的感染率最高。H9 是主要亚型,多种亚型共同循环。所有48个H9N2亚型分离株均属于G57基因型,血凝素(HA)和神经氨酸酶(NA)基因属于Y280样分支,而内部基因则呈现出G1样和F/98样谱系相结合的镶嵌模式。分子特征分析揭示了多个哺乳动物适应性突变,涉及受体结合位点(T163N、H191N、T197D、T198V、Q234L、Q235M)、抗原表位(D280G、N285S)和糖基化位点(218NRTF、313NCSK)的改变。NA 茎缺失 (62–64 aa),以及血细胞吸附位点中的多个 突变(E/K368N、D369S/G、D401G/V、N402D、W403L/R、Q432H)。此外,还在内部蛋白质中发现了多个关键氨基酸取代。结论 浙西外部环境中AIV 患病率 较高,且时空聚集性明显。H9 是主要亚型,并与多种亚型共同传播,活禽市场和屠宰场被确定为高风险环境。H9N2亚型AIV积累了多个哺乳动物适应性突变,并在中国东部省份表现出遗传联系。这些发现共同强调需要一个综合的 One Health 监测 和预警系统来降低人类感染 禽流感 的风险。

papers.title: Co-detection of highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) and SARS-CoV-2 in a bobcat ( Lynx rufus ), Washington, 2025
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) are important One Health pathogens with expanding host ranges. We describe an investigation of a bobcat ( Lynx rufus ) in Washington State in which HPAI H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b (genotype D1.1) and SARS-CoV-2 were co-detected. Clinical signs, diagnostic findings, and pathology were consistent with H5N1 infection. This report highlights the importance of integrated wildlife surveillance to characterize emerging zoonotic pathogens at the human-wildlife interface. IMPORTANCE This report documents the co-detection of two One Health threats, avian influenza and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, in a bobcat admitted to a wildlife rehabilitation facility. Although rare, the simultaneous detection of these viruses highlights gaps in routine monitoring of mammals and illustrates how wildlife may serve as bridging hosts for pathogens across the human-animal interface. Strengthening coordinated surveillance efforts is essential for understanding disease dynamics, protecting animal and public health, and supporting broader One Health preparedness strategies.

We describe an investigation of a bobcat ( Lynx rufus ) in Washington State in which HPAI H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b (genotype D1.1) and SARS-CoV-2 were co-detected. Clinical signs, diagnostic findings, and pathology were consistent with H5N1 infection. This report highlights the importance of integrated wildlife surveillance to characterize emerging zoonotic pathogens at the human-wildlife interface. IMPORTANCE This report documents the co-detection of two One Health threats, avian influenza and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, in a bobcat admitted to a wildlife rehabilitation facility. Although rare, the simultaneous detection of these viruses highlights gaps in routine monitoring of mammals and illustrates how wildlife may serve as bridging hosts for pathogens across the human-animal interface. Strengthening coordinated surveillance efforts is essential for understanding disease dynamics, protecting animal and public health, and supporting broader One Health preparedness strategies.

papers.title: Protective Efficacy Evaluation of Various Inactivated Vaccines Against the Newly Circulated Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Virus H5N1 of Clade 2.3.4.4b in Pekin Ducks
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus H5N1of clade 2.3.4.4b has emerged as the predominant lineage circulating in poultry flocks worldwide, raising concerns regarding the protective efficacy of currently available commercial vaccines, particularly in domestic ducks, which play an important role in virus maintenance and transmission. Thus, this study evaluated the immunogenicity along with the protective efficacy of four inactivated H5 vaccines against a recently isolated local HPAI-H5N1 (Newvalley-3-H5N1-2024, clade 2.3.4.4b) strain in Pekin ducks in Egypt. A total of 150 seronegative ducks were divided into vaccinated and control groups (10 groups) and vaccinated at 10 days of age. At 31 days of age, the vaccinated and positive control groups were challenged using 106.5 EID50/0.5 mL/duck with the local isolate (Newvalley-3-H5N1-2024) via the oculo-nasal route. The vaccine efficacy was assessed through clinical signs, survival rate, hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody titer, tracheal and cloacal viral shedding quantified by real-time RT-PCR, and histopathological examination of trachea, lung, pancreas, and brain tissues. Generally, all ducks vaccinated with the ValleyVac Avian Flu H5 plus and MEFLUVACTM H5 PLUS 8 showed a significantly higher survival rate (100%) at 10 days post-vaccination (DPV) than those in the positive control (66.7% mortality rate). In contrast, ducks exhibited mortality rates ranging from 6.7% in the SERVAC Flu H5N1 group to 13.4% in the Sinder Fluvac group. The ValleyVac Avian Flu H5 plus and MEFLUVACTM H5 PLUS 8 vaccines induced the highest HI antibody titers at 7, 14, 21, and 28 DPV in both homologous and heterologous AIV antigens, resulting in a significant reduction in viral load among all vaccinated duck groups (p-value
